evidence.scope: Actual HttpModelProvider through loopback synthetic HTTP service; actual Application, Engine, Vault and in-memory SQLite. No ScriptedModelProvider, real credentials, paid model, production DB or business MCP. No build performed.

findings.title: Negated requests and staging nouns grant execution intent
findings.trigger: In compose mode submit 保存草稿，不要发布或执行 or 创建试运行流程并保存草稿.
findings.actual: Both produce [edit_draft, run]. The actual HTTP provider receives workflow_start/advance/cancel and a returned workflow_start is executed to COMPLETED, despite the negative instruction. 请解释当前流程的运行原理 similarly grants edit_draft and run.
findings.impact: An LLM mistake or injected tool content can start a workflow including production queries when the user only requested a saved draft. The existing assistant fixture uses the same negative sentence but hardcodes actions=[edit_draft], hiding the UI classifier defect.
findings.fix: Resolve explicit action intent conservatively with negation/coordinated clauses and noun boundaries; do not derive run from 试运行/运行原理. Enforce the same intent envelope server-side. Keep positive combined create/publish/run requests supported without approval nodes.
findings.tests: Exercise the real shared classifier and full HTTP-provider task for Chinese/English positive, negative, coordinated negative, staging noun and explain-only sentences; assert absence of run tools and zero run records.

findings.title: Selected workflow scope does not restrict workflow_start or workflow_cancel
findings.trigger: Select workflow selected and ask to run the current flow; provider returns workflow_start(workflowId=other).
findings.actual: The task completes and the actual run belongs to other. The scope guard checks only draft_patch and draft_publish. workflow_cancel has no selected-run guard either; workflow_advance checks owner/kind but not context.runId.
findings.impact: The execution identity has global access, so one request can affect a different saved workflow/run than the user selected. This violates contextual action intent even though Engine owner checks still run.
findings.fix: Bind start/publish/edit/test and run mutations to explicit targets resolved from user intent/current selection; require runId equal the selected or task-created run for advance/cancel. Apply target checks before ledger dispatch. Do not silently grant all execution-owned runs.
findings.tests: Two different synthetic published flows and active runs; ask to run/cancel selected A while provider calls B; assert INTENT_NOT_ALLOWED, B untouched, A remains usable.

findings.title: Help-mode run context sends an execution credential to the model and permits cleartext persistence
findings.trigger: Choose a WAITING_AGENT run and ask only for an explanation in help mode.
findings.actual: engine.status includes checkpoint.token; it is serialized verbatim into Selected context and transmitted to the loopback model. When the synthetic model echoes that supplied token, the exact token appears in ordinary assistant_messages and plaintext application_events, even though the tool ledger separately encrypts tokenDelivery. Read-only workflow_status tool results also feed raw output to the model.
findings.impact: A client execution credential crosses an unnecessary external-model boundary and the encrypted-at-rest guarantee is broken through responses/events. This is separate from preserving original business data.
findings.fix: Create a model-safe run/checkpoint projection that omits the actual execution token in context and all tool results. Keep the credential inside daemon execution state and inject it immediately before authorized workflow_advance, using opaque checkpoint references. Do not apply business-data redaction.
findings.tests: Capture actual HTTP provider requests for help and compose; assert current and historical checkpoint credentials absent. Echo all supplied context and verify messages/events/ledger ordinary JSON never contain raw execution credentials; authorized advance still works.

findings.title: Deleting a session leaves event copies and analysis-tool ledger orphans
findings.trigger: Complete a normal assistant task or analysis task, then delete its session.
findings.actual: Normal task and messages disappear but its message.delta/task.completed events still stream from application_events. Reproduction leaves two events containing the synthetic echoed credential. The analysis ledger is created without sessionId at line 131, so deleteSession's sessionId filter leaves one assistant_tool_calls row after the analysis task is deleted.
findings.impact: Delete does not remove the durable copies the user asked to remove; business results and credential echoes can remain indefinitely. Cross-domain coordination needed with root-owned retention remediation.
findings.fix: Determine all taskIds before deleting the session; delete tool calls by taskId and owned event copies atomically, including analysis tasks. Preserve unrelated run data and unrelated sessions.
findings.tests: Real analysis plus normal session tasks with distinctive synthetic business strings; delete the sessions, replay SSE from cursor 0 and inspect all ledger rows; assert no deleted copies/orphans and unrelated records retained.

findings.title: Successful analysis submission cannot be retried with the same idempotency key
findings.trigger: POST analysis succeeds but client loses the response; retry the identical runId/profileId/key after checkpoint was advanced.
findings.actual: Reproduction first task COMPLETED and run SUCCEEDED; identical retry throws HOST_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE because current checkpoint validation executes before repo.command can return the persisted acceptance.
findings.impact: An ordinary transport retry reports a failed operation after it actually succeeded, breaking the promised shared idempotent task API. A changed profile with reused key may also return the wrong state error instead of IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
findings.fix: Perform idempotency lookup and request-hash validation before checking current checkpoint state; return the original accepted task without reanalysis or advancing another checkpoint.
findings.tests: Retry exact analysis request during generation, after success, after failure, after cancellation, and after a second checkpoint appears. Same key yields same task, changed content yields IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and no duplicate provider call.

findings.title: A usable non-streaming model is unusable through the formal UI
findings.trigger: Configure a compatible provider supporting text and tools but rejecting stream=true. Run model capability probes, then help-mode assistant.
findings.actual: Text and tools probes pass; stream probe fails; assistant still requests stream=true and fails MODEL_REQUEST_FAILED. The UI hardcodes stream:true and has no alternative. saveProfile also retains old capabilities/lastTestAt when model/provider/baseUrl changes.
findings.impact: A correctly configured usable text model cannot answer help through the product. Stale capability probes may block a newly selected capable model or misrepresent a replaced provider.
findings.fix: Expose stream selection or automatically use non-streaming after a failed/unsupported stream probe; keep actual tool capability gating independent. Reset capability tests when provider identity/model/protocol changes, and honor the new values.
findings.tests: Real loopback provider allows nonstream text/tools and rejects stream; formal profile settings and help/compose must work with truthful capability statuses. Retest/invalidate after changing model or URL.

findings.title: Timeout and body-read failures escape the Provider error contract
findings.trigger: Provider sends HTTP 200 headers and then stalls past profile.timeoutMs, either in JSON body or SSE body.
findings.actual: The synthetic 1000 ms timeout throws raw DOMException TimeoutError code 23 from response.json, outside the fetch try/catch. Assistant maps it to MODEL_CONNECTION_FAILED; analysis maps it to MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID. Task deadline abort is also reported as user CANCELLED rather than timeout/budget.
findings.impact: Timeouts are misdiagnosed and clients cannot distinguish cancellation, invalid model output and stalled network. The same response-read gap leaves nonstream responses without the stream path's 4 MiB budget.
findings.fix: Wrap fetch plus complete body consumption in one typed adapter boundary; distinguish user cancel, task deadline, provider timeout, invalid JSON and interrupted network; enforce a body budget for nonstream as well.
findings.tests: Headers-then-stall and mid-SSE stall, request timeout before headers, user abort, truncated JSON and oversized JSON; assert exact typed errors and zero tool dispatch.

findings.title: Analysis UI permanently disables retry and can disable the next analysis checkpoint
findings.trigger: Submit an analysis task that fails authentication/schema, or reach another analysis checkpoint in the same mounted run view.
findings.actual: setTask stores only acceptance; the control never polls/subscribes to task status and disables the action with disabled={!profile||task}. The failed result is never shown, changing profile cannot retry, and task state is not reset by runId/checkpointId changes.
findings.impact: A recoverable analysis failure or the standard second-analysis stage requires a full page reload; the interface cannot explain or cancel the pending task.
findings.fix: Track accepted task through the shared SSE/task-status service, display terminal errors and cancellation, re-enable on terminal failure, and reset state when run/checkpoint changes while retaining the original task receipt.
findings.tests: Playwright: model 401 then select valid profile/retry without reload; consecutive local analysis nodes; switch runs with task state present; cancel and retry while original checkpoint remains valid.

findings.title: Tool knowledge citations carry hashes of invented excerpt text rather than the cited file range
findings.trigger: Search workflow_draft_create and verify its citation against contracts/mcp-v2-tool-inputs.schema.json lines 735–786.
findings.actual: Citation.contentHash hashes name + space + description, while sourcePath/lineStart/lineEnd refer to JSON source with the full definition. The actual cited range has a different hash. Markdown chunks do hash their real range.
findings.impact: Version/staleness verification cannot verify tool citations as real source evidence; synthetic assembled content is presented with the same citation contract as source excerpts.
findings.fix: Build tool excerpts from the actual cited source range and hash those exact bytes, or define a separate normalized-content hash and source-range hash explicitly. Keep line numbers and actual source text coherent.
findings.tests: For every returned citation, read the exact source range and compare content/hash; also rebuild changed docs and identify old citations as stale. Preserve independent Chinese recall and mixed error-code tests.

designNotImplemented.requirement: 07 UI section 5 and UI-04: three-way local patch merge for nonconflicting fields, per-node/field conflict values and selective resolution
designNotImplemented.actual: All local dirtiness produces a whole-draft conflict; UI only offers compare, save-as and discard/reload. Inputs are preserved, but there is no same-revision nonconflicting merge or per-field keep-local/remote resolution.

designNotImplemented.requirement: 02 sections 6.4/6.5 and 07 section 6: select a run/artifact as assistant context with visible source/size and navigable knowledge citations
designNotImplemented.actual: The only formal AssistantPanel contexts are empty AI workspace and workflowId/revision/selectedNodeIds in editor. No UI passes runId/artifactRefs; citation cards display path/line/hash only and do not navigate to actual local help/source. Backend-only run context cannot be selected in the interface.

designNotImplemented.requirement: 02 sections 6.2/6.3 and 07 section 7: configurable timeout/limits/budget and accurate task usage
designNotImplemented.actual: Profile DTO has timeoutMs but formal model form does not expose it or budgets; per-task limits are hardcoded. usage is overwritten on every turn instead of accumulating, so two 7-token responses display 7 rather than 14. Unknown accounting for partial/failed turns has no representation.

designNotImplemented.requirement: 03 assistant messages history pagination and 02 storage strategy
designNotImplemented.actual: Messages silently return the last 100 with no cursor or older-history retrieval. Every new component subscription starts SSE at 0; browser Last-Event-ID handles reconnect only during that EventSource lifetime, not remounts. Root separately owns durable retention for V2 copies.

Analysis claim expires 180 s after acceptance, but each of up to three JSON/schema attempts receives a new 180 s AbortSignal; no total analysis deadline/lease renewal. Long retries may continue after claim expiry. Live long-duration scenario not executed.

Responses store:false continuation preserves raw output items but does not request reasoning.encrypted_content. Need official protocol verification plus a stateless reasoning-model-shaped synthetic continuation test before claiming a real provider defect. No paid model invoked.

429 currently stops after one request, records retryAfter only in the thrown details, and task final state keeps only errorCode. Design LLM-03 requests bounded cancellable retry; current code avoids infinite retries but does not implement Retry-After recovery.
